recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit as-is. No FHIR-18685 follow-up is needed unless the work group separately revisits persisted expansion or workflow-status behavior.
issue_request: FHIR-18685 asked to align ValueSet.status with VSD Activity Status by removing the old VSD 11 invariant, keeping the ValueSet.status name, clarifying that ValueSet.status applies to ValueSet.compose and associated non-expansion metadata, and adding that value set expansions are stateless to the ValueSet.expansion comments. Jira status is Published with resolution Persuasive with Modification.
initial_application: Jira records implementation in commit fbcbcb6ac4f574b7f9859cc6bf36e54befb5d312, titled "GF#18685 - remove vsd-11 and update definitions". Targeted history checks showed that commit added the status definition sentence and expansion-stateless comment to source/valueset/valueset-spreadsheet.xml before later source refactoring.
additional_context: ValueSet is active in source/fhir.ini. The current ValueSet StructureDefinition says status applies to ValueSet.compose and associated metadata and that expansions do not have a state; the expansion comment says expansions are stateless and explains the term. The current VSD notes also align ActivityStatus with ValueSet.status except for ValueSet.expansion. The remaining current vsd-11 key is a later FHIR-29821 designation.additionalUse invariant, not the removed status/expansion invariant. FHIR-36015 later added compatible VSD-aligned guidance. Confluence minutes confirm the 2018 motion, and Zulip/community searches found no conflicting later decision.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The seed request is already represented in active current source, and changing the later unrelated designation vsd-11 constraint would be wrong.

related_jiras.note: Later ValueSet designation.additionalUse work introduced the current vsd-11 constraint, explaining why a vsd-11 key still appears in current source.
